hypothesis: evm2's build.rs picks its interpreter dispatch backend at build time: explicit-tail-call (tco) on a nightly rustc, otherwise the packed backend (crates/evm2/build.rs DispatchBackend::resolve). build.sh uses stable, so the node runs the packed dispatcher. A nightly toolchain switches it to tco, which turns the opcode dispatch loop into tail calls. Expect a small heavy-phase gain; the toolchain change also moves codegen, so a nightly control is needed if it wins.
llm_commentary: A nightly toolchain measures 4.63s against the round's 4.72s control, -1.9%. evm2's build.rs picks its explicit-tail-call interpreter dispatch only on nightly (DispatchBackend::resolve), so this is the tco dispatcher replacing the packed one — but the toolchain change also moves all other codegen, so the delta is not attributable to dispatch alone, and -1.9% sits at the edge of Graviton5's +-3% drift. It is well short of the PGO+THP champion (4.31s), so nightly is not the fastest path on its own; the question worth answering is whether tail-call dispatch is independent of PGO's block layout, which exp-nightly-pgo-thp tests by stacking all three. Worth noting the practical cost either way: a nightly toolchain is a harder sell for a release build than a PGO pass.
